title: Hickory Chicken with Red-Eye Gravy and Soft Grits
description: A splash of decaf coffee gives hickory-braised chicken a toasty Southern gravy for a bowl of soft grits.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

steps.title: Heat the pellet smoker
steps.text: Load the Traeger Silverton 610 with hickory wood pellets. Preheat with the lid closed to 275°F, allowing about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Perfume the coffee broth
steps.text: Bring {broth}, {coffee}, {molasses} and {paprika} to a simmer in the Dutch oven on the stovetop. Transfer to the smoker grate with the pot uncovered and close the smoker lid for 8 minutes.

steps.title: Braise the chicken
steps.text: Place {chicken} flat in the hot coffee broth and spoon the broth over each thigh. Fit the pot lid immediately as the wrap point. Cook at 275°F for 30–45 minutes, checking from 25 minutes until each thigh reaches 175°F.

steps.title: Cook the soft grits
steps.text: While the thighs braise, bring {grits_water} to a boil in the saucepan. Whisk in {grits} and simmer on low for 5–8 minutes, stirring often until tender and spoonable.

steps.title: Enrich the grits
steps.text: Stir {butter} into the grits. Keep covered off heat until the gravy is ready.

steps.title: Rest in the braising liquid
steps.text: Transfer the chicken and a ladle of its liquid to a warm bowl. Cover and rest for 5 minutes while finishing the sauce.

steps.title: Concentrate the gravy
steps.text: Pour the braising liquid into the HexClad. Simmer until it measures about 1 1/4 cups, checking after 2 minutes.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Divide the grits between shallow bowls. Slice the chicken across the grain onto the grits and spoon the gravy and resting juices over both.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/4 cups of gravy for two, in addition to the grits. Make ahead: Brew the decaf the day before and refrigerate it. Cook the grits fresh if possible. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze the sliced chicken in its gravy for up to 2 months. Freeze the grits separately and loosen them with water as they warm. Fridge reheat: Warm the grits and sauced chicken covered in separate pans, adding a splash of water to the grits. Stir on medium-low and check from 6 minutes until both reach 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses a little decaf coffee. For gentler Option B, use additional broth for the coffee and sweet unsmoked paprika. For dairy-free grits, use avocado oil in place of the butter. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 310 kcal, 31.0 g protein, 21.9 g total carbohydrate, 10.1 g fat, 1.1 g fiber, 167 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth.
